description: Open-air Hindu street shrine of the Erawan type -- a gilded four-faced deity image under a small open pavilion on a raised platform, ringed with garlands and offered elephant figures.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small open-air shrine pavilion on a raised square platform, four slender gilded columns carrying a tiered pointed canopy roof with no walls, a gilded four-faced seated deity figure on a pedestal at the centre, dense marigold garlands looped over the pedestal and railing, rows of small carved wooden elephant figures massed on the platform edge, low railing with candle and incense trays around the outside Materials: Bright gold leaf on the figure and columns, fresh orange and browning marigold garlands, dark oiled teak elephants, thick candle wax runs and ash on the trays, polished granite platform.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: Rebuild 2026-08-31. The deity's four arms are modelled, reversing a declared omission on new evidence: the arms were left out because the single plate hides them behind garlands, and the reference proxy -- which was never consulted for this -- resolves a seated figure with arms spread at shoulder height. formDetail 0.66 -> 0.78, the lowest layer score in the kit. Merged into the existing deity-body geometry so draw calls and unique geometries stay at 11 of 12; 10,704 -> 11,312 of 16,000 triangles. The head's facial relief stays unmodelled because the proxy gives no evidence for it. Turntable reads holed at all four azimuths, which is correct and is the open-pavilion case -- the bays between the columns and the gaps between the balusters ARE background. check-coplanar reports 12 pre-existing hip-ridge-cap pairs that also reproduce on the bundle at HEAD; recorded, not introduced.

featureReviews.evidence: Four gilt columns carrying a concave-flared hip roof over an open deck, balustraded on all four sides.
Concave-flared hip roof with timber fascia band and four gilt hip ridge caps.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged. NOTE A LATENT DEFECT, pre-existing and not introduced here: check-coplanar reports 12 same-facing coplanar pairs at y=5.342 between hip-ridge-caps instances #2 and #3, 2.14 m2 each. It reproduces on the bundle committed at HEAD, so it has shipped in this state; the caps are an InstancedMesh, which is why one authoring mistake is reported as twelve pairs. Fixing it means offsetting alternate caps, and it is left recorded rather than silently carried.

featureReviews.evidence: 48 votive elephant figurines, 12 per side, embedded 0.015 m into the cap-slab ledge.
40 turned hardwood balusters, 10 per side, on top and bottom rails.
A four-sided head block with a tiered crown stepping to a spire, no facial relief.
featureReviews.notes: DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, and the reason matters because the sibling omission next to it WAS reversed. The head's facial relief is a declared omission -- 'only one of the four faces is legible in the plate' -- and unlike the arms it has no new evidence behind it: the reference proxy resolves the head as a crowned block and does not resolve faces on it at any usable resolution. The arms were reinstated because the proxy DID resolve them; the faces are not, because it did not. Scoring this feature up without that evidence would be inventing a measurement, so it stays at 0.55.

featureReviews.evidence: A seated figure with four arms merged into the deity-body geometry: a front pair coming out and down to hands resting on the lap, and a rear pair held out at shoulder height and lifted slightly, each with a shoulder ball and a hand.
featureReviews.notes: NEW, AND IT OVERTURNS A DECLARED OMISSION ON NEW EVIDENCE. This component was a bare lathe -- a solid of revolution that renders as a turned vase -- under a component named 'Seated four-armed deity figure' and a written note that the arms were unmodelled because they are 'occluded by garland masses in the only view available so there is no evidence for them' (unk-deity-arms, confidence 0.3). That was true of the PLATE and false of the reference mesh: the proxy's front elevation shows a seated figure with a crowned head and arms spread symmetrically at shoulder height, which settles their number and their gesture. A four-armed seated Brahma is canonical besides. The arms merge into the deity's OWN geometry rather than becoming a component, because this prop sits at 11 of 12 draw calls and 11 of 12 unique geometries while having 5,296 triangles spare -- so it costs triangles, which are free here, and not the last slot on the two axes that are not. `three` is the only permitted import, so BufferGeometryUtils is unavailable and the merge is hand-rolled through toNonIndexed. First pose ran the rear pair above the shoulder and two thirds of the lap's half-width out and read as a man surrendering; tucked to shoulder height.

name: Brahman Street Shrine
nameTh: ศาลพระพรหม
notes: An open-air shrine, so it has no walls at all -- four columns, a canopy roof and an open platform. That openness is the point and must not be closed in, because the deity figure has to be visible from the street on every side. The massed small elephant figures and the looped garlands are accumulated offerings and are what distinguishes this from a plain pavilion, so they are part of the asset rather than separate dressing. This is a Hindu Brahman shrine and its four-faced seated figure is deliberately not a Buddha image. Declared at 6 m, just below the building-part category's 8 m prior. No destruction groups: it is static landmark geometry.
